frames.narration: A sale has started and a buyer clicks checkout. The request reaches an edge load balancer. In this model it runs two jobs from Shopify's posts: Sorting Hat finds which pod owns the shop and adds a header, and the checkout throttle decides whether the buyer may pass.

The bucket for this 5 second period is full. The buyer is not shown an error. They get a waiting page cached at the edge, and a signed cookie holding the time of their first attempt, so that later the load balancer can tell how early they came.

The page keeps polling the checkout endpoint. Each load balancer works out a threshold on its own from the room in the bucket. This buyer's time is now below it, so the request goes through the leaky bucket, and the buyer gets a signed cookie to skip the throttle for the rest of the session.

The app server reads the pod header and connects only to that pod's datastores. Other pods are not involved, so a rush on this shop cannot use up their database time, and a failure here cannot stop them.

Now the session store is slow. Semian lets only a few workers wait on it and the rest fail at once, and after repeated failures the circuit breaker opens. The buyer is treated as a guest and the checkout carries on.

Later the active data center has a problem. Each pod has a recovery data center, and Shopify says its Pod Mover can move a pod there in about a minute without dropping requests or jobs. This model shows the move as one message.
